description:
SQL (DuckDB) over SEC filing data, for questions ACROSS MANY COMPANIES or filings: totals,
comparisons, breakdowns, screens, and finding which filings to read. For one company or one
filing use the other tools instead (get_filings, get_financial_history, get_filing_item...):
they pick the right tags and documents, derive quarters and link every figure, which SQL here
does not. Typical use: find the set with SQL, then read or verify each one with the other tools.
Three datasets today:
- filings: every EDGAR filing since 1993 (form, date, CIKs, 8-K Items, headline, fiscal
  period), each filing's files and exhibits, where each Item of a 10-K/10-Q/8-K/20-F is,
  and companies by SIC code, ticker and exchange. E.g. "the latest 10-Q of every listed
  grocery chain", "8-Ks with Item 4.02 by year", "424B5s filed in February 2024 and the
  issuer's 8-K within 5 days". It finds filings; read them with get_filing_item /
  search_document.
- formd: Form D exempt offerings since 2008, every field, with the rules for reading amounts
  ("money raised by California biotechs this year against last year, by quarter").
- xbrl: every XBRL fact in every 10-K, 10-Q, 20-F and 40-F since 2009 as filed (~376M), with
  the taxonomies' labels and definitions: compare one tag across companies ("the LIFO charge
  of every listed grocer, by quarter"), or find who reports a figure. Values as filed: no
  derived quarters, no standardization; join to filings by accession_number and cik.

Three steps:
1. No arguments: the datasets available, their form types, tables and how recent they are.
2. form="D", form="filings" or form="xbrl" (a form type or dataset name; any other form
   type gives the filing index): its tables, every field with its type and meaning, the values of its
   category fields, and the rules for reading it. Always read this before querying a
   dataset, and follow its rules.
3. sql="SELECT ...": one DuckDB SELECT (WITH is fine) over every dataset at once; tables need
   no prefix and may be joined. 15 seconds, at most 1,000 rows back: aggregate in SQL.

Each result names the snapshot it ran on (data_through, view_versions): the data is as of the
last nightly build, so state that date with the answer. Every figure is what the filer
reported to the SEC; the SEC does not check Form D.
A filing on sec.gov: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/<CIK without leading zeros>/<accession without dashes>/

Args:
    form: A form type ("D", "Form D/A") or dataset name; returns its tables, fields and rules
    sql: One DuckDB SELECT to run
name: query_sec
title: Query SEC data (SQL)
